title: fix(agents): working timer restarts when reopening a claude-cli session
body:
Related: #119728

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI "Working... Ns" timer restarts from about 1s every time you reopen or reload a session whose turn runs on the claude-cli runtime.

## User Impact

User impact: the working timer shows the real elapsed time of a long claude-cli turn after a session switch, reload or mobile page restore, instead of resetting to zero.

## Why This Change Was Made

#119729 added `startedAt` to the `chat.history` in-flight snapshot, taken from the active run owner. When a logical turn hands off to the CLI runtime, the deferred lifecycle manager registers a new owner handle without `startedAtMs`, so the snapshot has no `startedAt` and the UI falls back to now. This records the turn start when the lifecycle manager is created and puts it on the CLI owner. The time belongs to the whole turn, so retries and fallbacks before the handoff are counted too.

## Evidence

- Live check on a long claude-cli run: `chat.history` returned `inFlightRun` with `runId`, `text`, `sessionAbortable: true` and no `startedAt`.
- New regression test "keeps the logical turn start time on the CLI owner" (fake clock, 5 minutes between manager creation and CLI handoff, checks the owner `startedAtMs`). Fails before the fix (`undefined`), passes after.
- `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/deferred-lifecycle-owner.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed, about 46s on a shared box.
- No UI code changes; the UI already uses `startedAt` when the server sends it.


### After-fix proof on a real claude-cli turn

A gateway running 2026.9.6 plus this exact patch, during a long claude-cli turn (it had been running for about an hour). Two `chat.history` reads 22 seconds apart, which is the call the Control UI makes when you reopen or reload the session:

```
$ openclaw gateway call chat.history --json \
    --params '{"sessionKey":"<claude-cli session>","limit":1}' \
  | jq -c '.inFlightRun | {hasRunId: (.runId != null), startedAt, startedAtIso: (.startedAt/1000|todate), sessionAbortable}'
13:36:50 UTC  {"hasRunId":true,"startedAt":1791117494647,"startedAtIso":"2026-10-04T12:38:14Z","sessionAbortable":true}
13:37:12 UTC  {"hasRunId":true,"startedAt":1791117494647,"startedAtIso":"2026-10-04T12:38:14Z","sessionAbortable":true}
```

Before the fix the same snapshot had no `startedAt` (first Evidence bullet), so the UI fell back to now and the timer restarted at about 1s. After the fix `startedAt` is the real turn start (12:38:14 UTC) and stays the same across reads, so a reopened session shows about 58 minutes of working time instead of restarting.


### Maintainer verification on the exact PR head

Kept rogeriochaves’ patch unchanged at `a41bc25937af31417254a93f40970943d1839f42`. No overlap with Pash/Sarah changes.

- Built isolated Gateways on current main `88934753a4927f8dbcef374277e6f757b464ae75` and the PR head, using a synthetic `claude` executable that streams for 25 seconds (no Anthropic credentials). Started turns through the Gateway `agent` method and read `chat.history` twice using the shipped CLI. Both main snapshots lacked `startedAt`; both candidate snapshots retained `1791139253930`. An observational clock trace recorded that exact value at logical-turn lifecycle creation.
- The embedded-provider control retained its start timestamp across history reads. Completed CLI and embedded turns no longer exposed `inFlightRun`.
- Ran the PR’s regression file against both versions: main fails the added case with `expected undefined to be 1000000` (14 pass, 1 fail; 24.95s wall); candidate passes all 15 (26.45s wall). These runs used the repository test wrapper with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- The exact candidate Gateway completed one real `openai/gpt-5-mini` request with reasoning `low` and a configured 4096-token output budget. History showed the active run, then the final assistant response with `stopReason: stop`, 658 output tokens, and no remaining `inFlightRun`.
- Existing exact-head CI is green and ClawSweeper is ready with no findings. No CI reruns, code repush, or changelog changes.
